correctness.rationale: The geometry reduces area to a sum of pairwise absolute determinants. Conditioning on one generator yields the exact first Hoeffding projection; the remaining degenerate pairs have exact orthogonal variances. The uniform-direction |sin| Fourier expansion and finite-coordinate CLT yield the exponential series, with L2 tail bounded by 4r^4/pi^2 times sum of squared coefficient denominators, uniformly in n. With bounded radial noise, the triangular degenerate-kernel difference has L2 norm O(n^{1-beta}), proving the three scales. Independence at beta=1/2 follows from independent directions and radii. Standalone tests verify 126 convex-hull examples, exact Fourier constants, 22k triangular simulation cases and exact finite-n covariance identities. Infinite claims rely on the proof, not sampling.

originality.rationale: The complete triangular-array area crossover including the independent Gaussian-plus-exp-series law at radial noise n^{-1/2}, with its exact finite-n variance identity and sharp competing scales, was not found in the inspected literature or searched published records. Fixed-radius non-Gaussian behavior is explicitly not claimed original. Schneider 2022 addresses fixed generator laws and a nondegenerate U-statistic CLT; Silverman 1978 treats circle-distance empirical processes at a fixed distribution; de Wet 1987 provides generic degenerate U-stat theory. None of these inspected statements supplies the n-dependent radial perturbation or its independent critical convolution without additional triangular decomposition. Priority remains provisional, with clearly documented residual risks.

value.rationale: An iid uniform-direction segment model is a canonical random planar zonotope. Its deterministic-length case has non-Gaussian order-n area variability, whereas nonzero fixed radial spread causes order-n^(3/2) Gaussian variation. The precise variance-competition scale n^(-1/2) for radial length noise is mathematically forced by these orders; the exact independent convolution at this critical scale is a structural phase boundary, not an arbitrary parameter slice or a restatement of a generic fixed-law CLT. The exact variance formula permits calibration across all finite sizes.
